simple.meaning: טְעַם (ṭᵉʻam) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 4:22. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טְעַם (H2939) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows טְעַם through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: טְעַם (ṭᵉʻam) / H2939 is tracked through Daniel 4:22, Daniel 4:29, Daniel 5:2, Daniel 5:21. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

majorEvents.evidenceText: He was driven from the sons of men, and his heart was made like the animals’, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. He was fed with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky; until he knew that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and that he sets up over it whomever he will.

timeline.evidenceText: it is you, O king, that have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.
At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.

Belshazzar, while he tasted the wine, commanded that the golden and silver vessels which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem be brought to him; that the king and his lords, his wives and his concubines, might drink from them.
